c.tagline: Zimbabwe's jacaranda-lined capital of leafy avenues, galleries and markets.

taxi.color: no uniform colour; metered taxis are phoned, not hailed
taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis don't cruise for fares - order by phone or use a local ride-hailing app (Vaya, Hwindi, inDrive) and agree the price before setting off. Uber does not operate in Harare.

emergency.note: 999 and 112 route to police, fire and ambulance, though public response can be slow; many visitors rely on private ambulance services such as EMRAS or ACE Air & Ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Petty crime in the CBD; caution at night; avoid political gatherings

hood_desc: Harare's commercial heart, home to the National Gallery of Zimbabwe, Africa Unity Square and the famous jacaranda-lined avenues; lively by day and quiet after dark, with the bustling Mbare Musika market just to the south.
A leafy, walkable near-north suburb with the popular Avondale Shopping Centre and flea market, cafes, bookshops and restaurants; a relaxed, convenient base close to the University of Zimbabwe.
Harare's affluent northern suburb, with the upscale Sam Levy's Village and Borrowdale Village malls, the Borrowdale Park racecourse and many of the city's best hotels and restaurants.
A quiet, leafy upmarket residential and diplomatic area east of the centre, full of large gardens, embassies and guesthouses; calm and green, best for a peaceful stay.
A leafy inner suburb just northwest of the CBD lined with jacarandas, guesthouses and small hotels; a quiet yet central base within easy reach of both downtown and Avondale.
lodging: It's a Small World Backpackers Lodge

water.note: Municipal supply is unreliable and often untreated — drink bottled or filtered water.

transit.pay: Kombi and ZUPCO fares are paid in cash to the conductor (in USD or local ZiG); there is no fare card system. Metered taxis must be phoned rather than hailed, so most visitors use ride-hailing apps (Vaya, Hwindi, inDrive) or a hired driver.
transit.hours: Kombis run roughly 5am-8pm and thin out sharply after dark; there is no reliable night service, so arrange a driver or ride-hail app in the evening.
transit.note: Harare has no metro or commuter rail; the day-to-day network is privately run commuter omnibuses (kombis) plus state ZUPCO buses, both crowded and informally routed. Kombis are cheap but chaotic, so most visitors rely on hired drivers or ride-hailing apps.

train: National Railways of Zimbabwe (long-distance passenger service to Bulawayo/Mutare suspended since 2020)
bus: Intercity coaches to Bulawayo, Mutare and Victoria Falls, plus cross-border to South Africa and Zambia

transit.m: Pre-booked hotel shuttle or taxi (~20-30 min)

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants is appreciated; small USD tips for guides, drivers and porters are customary and often expected.

food.name: Sadza ne nyama
food.desc: Stiff white maize meal pudding eaten by hand with a stewed relish of beef, oxtail or chicken - Zimbabwe's national plate.

places.name: Gava's Restaurant
places.note: Open-air sports-club setting; sadza re zviyo with oxtail, covo and sugar beans.

places.name: Garwe Restaurant
places.note: The go-to address for indigenous Zimbabwean cooking, game meats included.

places.name: Paula's Place
places.note: Homely spot known for sadza with traditional sides at fair prices.

food.name: Muriwo une dovi
food.desc: Collard or pumpkin greens simmered down with thick peanut butter until creamy - the relish that makes a plate of sadza.

places.name: Gava's Restaurant
places.note: Covo and muriwo cooked the old way, in peanut butter rather than oil.

places.name: Garwe Restaurant
places.note: Full spread of indigenous vegetables alongside the meat dishes.

places.name: Paula's Place
places.note: Good vegetarian option; the greens come without a meat stock base.

food.name: Mazondo
food.desc: Cow trotters stewed for hours until the collagen turns to jelly, seasoned hard and eaten with sadza and a lot of napkins.

places.name: Gava's Restaurant
places.note: Mazondo is a house speciality and usually sells out at weekends.

places.name: Garwe Restaurant
places.note: Traditional cuts - trotters, tripe, oxtail - cooked without shortcuts.

places.name: Mereki
places.note: Legendary open-air braai yard where you buy meat and have it grilled on the spot.

food.name: Gochi gochi braai
food.desc: Beef, pork and boerewors grilled over open coals and eaten straight off the fire with sadza and chilli - Harare's weekend ritual.

places.name: Mereki
places.note: The city's most famous braai spot; loud, sociable and busy from Friday night.

places.name: Mokoto Meat Lounge
places.note: Strong nyama choma selection, grilled meat seasoned with local herbs.

places.name: Garwe Restaurant
places.note: Sit-down version of the braai with game meat on the grill.

food.name: Biltong
food.desc: Air-dried beef or game cured with coriander and vinegar, sliced thin; the southern African road-trip snack, sold by the gram.

places.name: Sam Levy's Village butcheries
places.note: Several butchers here cut biltong and droewors to order.

places.name: Avondale Shopping Centre
places.note: Long-standing butchery counters and a weekend flea market with biltong stalls.

places.name: Mokoto Meat Lounge
places.note: Butcher-restaurant combination, useful if you want biltong plus a hot meal.

food.name: Madora and kapenta
food.desc: Dried mopane worms fried with onion and tomato, and tiny Kariba kapenta fish crisped in oil - two Zimbabwean staples worth being brave for.

places.name: Mbare Musika
places.note: Harare's biggest market; the place to see madora, kapenta and dried greens sold in bulk.

places.name: Garwe Restaurant
places.note: One of the few sit-down kitchens that keeps madora on the menu.

places.name: Gava's Restaurant
places.note: Kapenta with sadza appears regularly on the daily specials board.

food.name: Maheu
food.desc: Lightly fermented maize drink, thick and faintly sour, sold chilled in cartons or ladled fresh; sustaining rather than refreshing.

places.name: Mbare Musika
places.note: Home-made maheu sold by the cup among the produce stalls.

places.name: Gava's Restaurant
places.note: Serves maheu alongside the traditional food, as it should be.

places.name: Garwe Restaurant
places.note: Commercial and traditional maheu both usually available.

food.name: Mazoe Orange Crush
food.desc: The bright orange cordial made in Zimbabwe since the 1920s, diluted with cold water and drunk by absolutely everyone.

places.name: Gava's Restaurant
places.note: Jugs of Mazoe on the table are practically standard with a sadza lunch.

places.name: Mbare Musika
places.note: Bottles sold everywhere in the market, cheapest place to stock up.

places.name: Sam Levy's Village
places.note: Supermarkets and cafes here carry the full range including the raspberry version.

landmarks: National Gallery of Zimbabwe
Zimbabwe's premier art institution showcases the country's world-famous Shona stone sculpture alongside contemporary African painting in leafy gardens beside Harare Gardens.
Epworth Balancing Rocks
Gravity-defying granite boulders stacked by millennia of erosion, once printed on Zimbabwean banknotes, rise from the savanna just southeast of the capital.
National Heroes Acre
A monumental North Korean-designed hillside shrine with a bronze Tomb of the Unknown Soldier honors Zimbabwe's liberation war heroes beneath a towering obelisk.
Mukuvisi Woodlands
Minutes from downtown, this 265-hectare reserve lets visitors walk or ride horseback among giraffe, zebra and eland beneath indigenous msasa trees.
Harare Gardens
The city's largest central park offers shaded lawns, a miniature Victoria Falls rainforest walk and colonial-era bandstand, a green lung beside the National Gallery.
Mbare Musika Market
Harare's oldest township hosts its most electrifying market, a sprawling bazaar of produce, mbira instruments, curios and kombis that reveals the city's true pulse.
Chapungu Sculpture Park
A serene outdoor gallery in Msasa displays monumental Shona stone carvings by Zimbabwe's master sculptors, with artists often at work on site.
Domboshava Rocks
Thirty kilometers north, this sacred granite dome shelters ancient San rock paintings and rewards a short climb with sweeping sunset views over the highveld.
The Kopje
Harare's historic granite hill, where the Pioneer Column first raised its flag in 1890, overlooks the entire city skyline from Africa Unity Square to Mbare.
National Botanic Garden
A forested reserve of native Zimbabwean woodland and the national herbarium in Alexandra Park, showcasing hundreds of indigenous plant species alongside collections from Asia and the Americas.

dom.op: National Railways of Zimbabwe — tickets at Harare station, no online booking

train.note: There are no working international passenger trains - the cross-border services to South Africa, Zambia and Mozambique have been suspended for years. Domestically, NRZ runs a slow overnight train between Harare and Bulawayo, taking around 12 hours when it runs; the network is run down and delays are routine. Tickets are sold at the station on the day, and there is no online booking.

intl.to: Johannesburg & Pretoria (South Africa) - via the Beitbridge border, ~16-18 hr

intl.op: Intercape / Pathfinder / regional operators — tickets at the Harare Road Port terminal

bus.note: Harare's Road Port on Fifth Street is the international coach terminal. Johannesburg takes sixteen to eighteen hours, with Beitbridge the notorious bottleneck - waits of several hours there are normal, and much longer around Christmas. Carry your passport and expect to pay border fees in cash. Domestic coaches to Bulawayo take about 6 hours and Victoria Falls 10-12.

ferry.note: Zimbabwe is landlocked and Harare is inland on the highveld, so there are no ferries. The Kariba ferry across Lake Kariba between Kariba town and Mlibizi runs as a scenic multi-day service in the north-west of the country, several hours away by road.

half.name: Domboshava Caves & Rock Art
half.blurb: Granite hill ~30 km north with ancient San rock paintings and sweeping views over the countryside.

half.name: Lake Chivero Recreational Park
half.blurb: Game park and reservoir ~35 km southwest with white rhino, zebra and giraffe, plus boating and picnicking.

full.name: Chinhoyi Caves National Park
full.blurb: Limestone cave system ~120 km northwest with the vivid cobalt-blue 'Sleeping Pool', a popular dive and photo spot.
